name: Dub-techno/house stab family: two detuned saws (osc 2 nudged toward square) into a resonant 24 dB low-pass at ~100 Hz with envelope amount ~48 and a 120 Hz high-pass, soft attack, hand-drawn cutoff automation that differs each repeat, dual resonant band-pass filters swept by a 1-2 bar LFO plus chorus, a long 'dub verb' return sidechained to the kick, a longer (6 s) verb and echoes automated up in breakdowns, all built on one four-note minor chord (root triad plus the note 2 semitones below the root)
goal: Build 3-5 call-and-response chord stabs that sound like one source and keep moving without any pitch randomness. Delta vs filter/phaser clusters: a full stab-family recipe in which the movement comes from drawn cutoff automation and dual band-pass sweeps rather than LFO-on-cutoff, with kick-sidechained reverb returns that pump with the groove and breakdown-only reverb-length automation.

source.title: Make Lush & Dubby Synths (Like Traumer, Kolter & Janaret)

prerequisites: A two-oscillator synth with a resonant LP and an HP filter and a mod matrix (any wavetable/VA synth)
A dual-filter or phaser effect, chorus, 2 long reverbs, delay/echo, sidechain compressor, glue compressor, saturator

inputs.name: kick
inputs.description: Kick for sidechaining the reverb return

outputs.name: stab_group
outputs.description: Grouped stab layers sharing returns, with breakdown automation

constraints: Pitch stays fixed: movement is drawn filter automation and filter/LFO sweeps only, with no random pitch or note variation (Matt's preference).
Use at most two chord types per track (e.g. Am add the note a tone below the root, plus Em).
Echo throws are sparse: no rapid repeats or clicking rolls.
Drums (kick) enter early (~8 counts / ~12 s) so the sidechained verb has something to pump against.

Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with Ableton, Reason, Bitwig, Soundtoys, FabFilter, Eventide or any vendor. Map product devices to generic modules (sampler, noise osc, filter, envelope, LFO, EQ, saturator, compressor, delay, reverb) in any DAW, hardware or Web Audio.
Steady pitch: no random pitch wobble or randomised notes; no rapid clicking textures (Matt's preference).

steps.action: Osc 1 saw, osc 2 saw with its wave position nudged toward square, and detune osc 2.
Filter 1: low-pass 24 dB, clean, high resonance, cutoff ~100 Hz. Filter 2: high-pass ~120 Hz to clear lows.
steps.expect: Dark resonant stab with no mud

steps.action: Amp envelope with a slightly softened attack; route an envelope to filter 1 cutoff (amount ~48). Use a longer decay for the main downbeat stab and shorter ones for answers.
steps.expect: Warm, non-harsh stab that opens and closes

steps.action: Draw cutoff automation by hand (or record a knob) and make each repeat's shape slightly different, instead of an LFO on cutoff.
steps.expect: Natural, evolving movement with pitch unchanged

steps.action: Insert a dual filter: two resonant band-pass filters with quite a lot of resonance (the auto-captions give the setting only as 'four'; set by ear), swept by a 1-2 bar LFO at ~50% depth; then a chorus. A phaser is a weaker substitute.
Chord: minor triad plus the note two semitones below the root (A minor: A C E + G below), optionally plus the 7th (B). Answer stabs reuse it with shorter notes, snappier envelopes and one osc.

Send all stabs to a 'dub verb' return (long, ~4 s, lush) sidechained to the kick; add echo; add a second, longer (~6 s) reverb whose send/decay rises in breakdowns; keep a third echo mainly for breakdowns.
steps.expect: Reverb pumps with the groove and swells in breakdowns

steps.action: Group the stabs: saturator for edge, insert reverb to glue, low-shelf cut on low mids, glue compressor at ~25% wet, and an auto filter that slopes down in the breakdown and reopens; finish with gentle tube warmth.
steps.expect: Stabs sound like one source; breakdown gets deeper then opens

verification: Only filter/FX parameters move; note pitches are fixed with no random modulation.
Reverb return gain-reduction meter moves with each kick hit.
No more than two chord types are used; the main chord contains the note a whole tone below the root.
